1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.Ng5 d5 5.e.name: Italian Game: Two Knights Defence, Ulvestad Variation
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.Ng5 d5 5.e.background: The American master Olav Ulvestad introduced 5...b5 in a 1941 article in Chess Review.

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.Ng5 d5 5.e.strategy: Counter-intuitive, but the only good answer: the bishop leaves the attacked square and guards g2, so a queen capture on d5 only loses time to a knight development that hits it. White keeps the extra pawn and the pressure on f7 while Black has to prove the compensation.
Chases the knight, but the sacrifice on f7 refutes it: after the king takes, the d-pawn captures the knight on c6, leaving White two pawns up against an exposed king.
